# Incident Report — 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| Logged-in domain user | `WIRESHARKWORKSHOP\ccollier` |
| AD domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (DC: WIRESHARK-WS-DC, 172.16.1.4) |
| OS (from malware beacon) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |

## Malware Family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/credential-stealer/keylogger).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The malware's proprietary C2 protocol transmits the literal ASCII string `STRRAT` in every beacon, along with its version number, e.g.:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

- Campaign/build ID: `1BE8292C`
- Reported malware version: `1.6`
- Protocol framing: each message is preceded by a plaintext ASCII length header terminated `\r\n\r\n` (e.g. `136\r\n\r\n`) followed by the pipe-delimited payload — no encryption on this channel.
- Beacon interval: ~5 seconds, continuously from frame 9066 (t=76.99s) through the end of the capture (t≈528s).
- The base64 field is the victim's active foreground window title (decoded values observed: `Documents`, `Home`, `Pictures`, `Program Manager`, `Fanad Head Lighthouse - Paint`, `pounds-formula [Compatibility Mode] - PowerPoint`), consistent with STRRAT's known window-title/keylogger reconnaissance behavior.
- Supporting behavioral indicator: the infected host queried `ip-api.com` (`GET /json/` to 208.95.112.1) using a spoofed `Chrome/73.0.3683.86` user agent shortly after infection (t=78s) — a known STRRAT self-geolocation routine, matching the `US:United States` field reported in the C2 beacons.
- Java-related lookups (`javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com`) and TLS sessions to `github.com`/`objects.githubusercontent.com`/`repo1.maven.org` around t=64s are consistent with a Java-based dropper/loader stage (STRRAT ships as a `.jar`), but the payload content was TLS-encrypted and could not be extracted from this capture (see IOC caveats below).

## Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-Control
| Type | Value |
|---|---|
| C2 IP:port | **141.98.10.79:12132** (plaintext TCP, no TLS, no DNS lookup preceded the connection — hardcoded IP) |
| Local source port | 49754 |
| First contact | t=76.99s (frame 9066), persists to end of capture |
| C2 domain | None observed — C2 connects directly to a raw IP with no DNS resolution |

### Malicious/Suspicious URLs
- `http://208.95.112.1/json/` (Host: `ip-api.com`) — self-geolocation lookup by the malware, not itself malicious infrastructure but a strong behavioral IOC of this STRRAT instance.

### Domains/Infrastructure Observed at/near Infection Time (legitimate services, possibly abused for staging — content not recoverable)
- `github.com` (140.82.113.3)
- `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133)
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) — 8.8 MB transferred, largest single conversation in the capture
- `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (23.194.164.136)

These four hosts were all contacted for the first time within a ~1-second window at t≈64–65s, immediately preceding the first STRRAT C2 beacon at t=77s — consistent with a Java loader fetching a runtime/dependency chain before executing the RAT. No file names or hashes could be extracted because all of this traffic is TLS-encrypted and no TLS keylog is available.

### Transferred Files / Hashes
**None recoverable.** `tshark --export-objects http` and `--export-objects smb` over the full capture yielded only benign artifacts:
- `connecttest.txt` (Microsoft NCSI check, harmless)
- `ip-api.com` JSON geolocation response
- Standard Group Policy files (`GptTmpl.inf`, `Registry.pol`, `gpt.ini`) pulled from SYSVOL via SMB — normal domain-joined workstation behavior, not malware artifacts.

No cleartext executable, JAR, or archive transfer was captured. All large transfers (GitHub, Maven Central, Oracle) rode over TLS 1.2/1.3 with no session keys logged in this pcap, so SHA256 hashes cannot be computed from this evidence alone.

## Summary
Host DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user `ccollier`, was infected with **STRRAT v1.6** (build `1BE8292C`). The malware beacons every ~5 seconds in plaintext to its C2 at **141.98.10.79:12132**, reporting hostname, username, OS, installed AV (Windows Defender), and the active foreground window — confirming keylogging/reconnaissance activity. Infection likely rode in via a Java-based loader that pulled staged content from GitHub/Maven Central/Oracle around t=64s, but that payload traffic was encrypted and unrecoverable from this capture.
